name: command
purpose: Command Menu is a ⌘K command palette: a modal overlay with a search input and a filtered, keyboard-navigable list of actions. It wraps the `Dialog` primitive for its panel, backdrop, focus trap, scroll-lock, and Escape handling, and adds the palette chrome on top — a search `Input`, a scrollable `List` of `Item`s organized into optional `Group`s, an `Empty` state, and `Separator`s. The root owns open/closed state (controlled or uncontrolled), a global open shortcut (⌘K / Ctrl+K), the ranked filter, nested pages, and roving active-item navigation. The filter is fuzzy and ranked: an item matches on its label (prefix, then word start, then anywhere, then an in-order abbreviation such as `dpl` for "Deploy"), its `value`, or its extra `keywords` (a keyword equal to the query, then one that starts with it, then one that contains it, all below any match in the label and above an abbreviation, since the reader cannot see why a keyword matched); better matches rise to the top of their group, groups rise by their best item, and while any label matches the query a group shows at most three matches that come only from its values or keywords (its best three), so a strong label match in a later group is not pushed under a run of hidden-keyword matches, and the matched characters of a plain-text label are emphasized. An item can open a `Page` — a nested list such as "Switch project" — with a back control in the search bar. It differs from `dropdown` (a small trigger-anchored menu) and `select` (a form value picker): Command Menu is a full-screen search-first launcher for actions, not a positioned menu or an input control.
useWhen: Use Command for the searchable ⌘K palette of actions and destinations; a short list of actions opened from a button is a DropdownMenu.
Provide a global ⌘K launcher for navigating to pages or running actions across an app.
Let users filter a large, grouped list of commands by typing, then activate with the keyboard.
avoidWhen: A small menu anchored to a trigger button → use `dropdown-menu`.
Picking a value for a form field → use `select` / `multi-select`.
A confirmation or content modal without search/list semantics → use `dialog` directly.
related: `dialog` — the overlay primitive Command Menu wraps for panel, backdrop, focus trap, and Escape.
`kbd` — renders each item's keyboard-shortcut hint and the ⌘K affordance.
`dropdown-menu` — trigger-anchored menu; reach for it when the list is short and positioned by a trigger.
bestPractices: Write items as Title Case verb phrases describing an action ("Deploy Project"), not navigation labels.
Keep the palette controlled via `v-model:open` so the app can open it from a button and from the global ⌘K shortcut.

Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.
Group related actions with `<Command.Group label="…">` and separate distinct sections with `<Command.Separator>`.
Give an item `keywords` for the words people type that are not in its label (`['org', 'team']` on "Switch organization"). Keywords match, they are never shown.
Use a `Page` for a choice that needs its own list ("Switch project", "Change theme"), not for a deep tree: pages are one stack, and every page is one Backspace away from the previous one.

props.name: dismissible
props.doc: When true, backdrop click and Escape close the palette.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: Global `'+'`-delimited keyboard shortcut that toggles the palette open (e.g. `'meta+k'`); matched against Ctrl on non-macOS platforms.

events.name: select
events.notes: Fires when an enabled item is activated (click or `Enter`). `event` is the activation event; `value` is the item's identifier. The palette closes automatically and focus returns to the element that was focused before opening.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The palette content: a `<Command.Input>` followed by a `<Command.List>`. Rendered inside the teleported dialog panel.
